# WorkLouderCTL

> WorkLouderCTL is an unofficial, open-source full-configuration CLI being built for Codex, Work Louder Input, and Codex Micro. It targets complete configuration-GUI parity with safe inspection, diff, backup, verified apply, synchronization, and rollback for humans, scripts, and AI agents.

Important: the project is currently a source alpha. The repository builds a working `worklouderctl` binary with Codex/Input inspection, offline semantic candidate editors, authenticated Codex/Input bridge clients, fixture-verified apply/readback/restore/rollback, live Codex Micro status/files, and verified exports, but there is no packaged release yet.

## Canonical facts

- Product name: WorkLouderCTL
- Repository: MarlinDiary/worklouder-input-cli
- Binary: worklouderctl (currently built from source)
- Product category: full-configuration CLI and command-line configurator
- Initial device target: Work Louder Codex Micro
- Initial host target: macOS
- Product goal: replace Codex and Input configuration GUIs for Codex Micro with complete typed CLI coverage
- Tier boundary: Tier 1 uses Codex authorities; Tier 2 and above use Work Louder Input authorities; the CLI configures every tier
- Provider strategy: delegate driver, BLE/HID, firmware, and host runtime behavior to the installed Codex/Input versions
- Non-goal: implementing a replacement hardware driver or firmware protocol
- Initial research baseline: Codex 26.727.51351, Work Louder Input 0.17.3/0.18.0, and Codex Micro firmware v0.6.0
- Public fixture boundary: deterministic synthetic Input 0.17.3/0.18.0 configuration snapshots and a firmware v0.6.0 status DTO, with regenerated SHA-256 manifests and sensitive-pattern checks
- Current maturity: source alpha; read paths and isolated bridge apply/restore transaction conformance implemented; no packaged release
- Current Codex commands: `codex doctor/inspect/export`, `codex bridge inspect`, `codex config snapshot/apply/restore`, six-slot `codex agent-key assignments/snapshot/get/set/clear/apply/restore`, `codex lighting brightness/auto-off get/set`, and `codex voice get/set`
- Codex Tier 1 candidates: `codex agent-source`, `codex agent-key tap-mode`, `codex command-key`, global lighting, and voice mode provide strict offline get/set/reset with deterministic revisions and source-SHA CAS receipts; six-slot Agent Key candidates preserve untargeted unknown fields and use a separate global-state revision; the Codex Companion Bridge fixture verifies complete settings and Agent Key apply/readback/restore/rollback while released-Codex integration remains pending
- Input cache command: `input config snapshot` captures `keymap.json` plus optional `smart_actions.json` byte-for-byte, excludes host-only state, and emits a bridge-revision-equivalent semantic snapshot without controlling the Input GUI or device transport
- Primary device transport: authenticated Input Companion Bridge v1 over a private Unix socket; Rust client, one-call Input-main integration, release conformance command, and cross-language tests are implemented
- Bridge config commands: deterministic byte-exact snapshot/validate plus capability-gated apply/restore with immutable CLI backup, CAS, session idempotency, full readback, and automatic rollback
- Released Input integration: pending; Input 0.18.0 has no external bridge transport
- Released Codex integration: pending; Codex 26.727.51351 has internal settings/global-state handlers but no external bridge listener
- Direct compatibility transport: `device status`, `device files`, and dual-hash atomic `device export` through Input 0.18.0's bundled device kit with `require-closed` or explicit `restart`
- Safety model: inspect, plan, diff, backup, conflict check, apply, readback, checksum verification, synchronize, rollback
- Agent model: deterministic JSON over the same transaction engine as the human CLI
- Affiliation: independent community project; not affiliated with Work Louder or OpenAI

## Terminology

Use “Work Louder Input” for the official GUI application, “Codex Micro” for the initial hardware target, “WorkLouderCTL” for this project, and “worklouderctl” for the planned command.
